section.sectionSummaryBrief: The sitra achra corresponds to holiness, and just as it has an eleventh level separate from ten, so too holiness has a level above the ten Sefiros that is separate from them, which is the encompassing level that is not counted with them, unlike in the sitra achra where the encompassing is their life-force and must be counted; thus the refinement of the eleven impurities is through drawing down the encompassing level above the Sefiros, like Atik, paralleling the eleventh level of the sitra achra, and this is the meaning of "Vayiten Lecha Elokim" beginning with dew, the dew of Atik.
section.t: Now, the sitra achra is parallel to this in holiness.
And from this it is understood,
that just as in impurity there is a level that is an eleventh that is separate from the ten,
so too in holiness there is parallel to this,
that there is a level that is above the ten Sefiros and separate from them.
[However, in holiness,
this level is not the life-force of the ten Sefiros
[for the life-force of the ten Sefiros is invested within them and unified with them as above.
And the encompassing level that is above the ten Sefiros is a matter unto itself19]
Therefore it is not counted with them,
"You are One and not in number"20,
but not so in the sitra achra,
where the encompassing level is their life-force,
it is necessary to include the encompassing in their count
(for without the encompassing they have no life-force21),
therefore they are eleven in number].
And based on this it is understood,
that the refinement of the eleven crowns of impurity is through the drawing down of the encompassing level that is above the ten Sefiros,
which is not counted with them
(the level of Atik22),
paralleling the eleventh level in the sitra achra that is separate from them as above.
And this is "Vayiten Lecha Elokim mital hashamayim,"
for the first matter in Yitzchak's blessing is dew,
the dew of Atika23,
because in order to refine the sparks that are in Eisav, it is through the drawing down of the level of Atik,
as above.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: For the drawing down of Atik below to refine the sparks of the sitra achra is specifically through the drawing down of the Essence of Ein Sof, which is above even Atik, since Atik by itself cannot be drawn down, and this is the superiority of Yitzchak's blessing "Vayiten Lecha Elokim" over "Vayevarech Elokim es Yitzchak," as it draws from the essential concealment of Ein Sof.
section.t: Now, in order for there to be a drawing down of Atik below, to the extent that through this there will be a refinement of the sparks in the sitra achra,
it is specifically through the drawing down of the Essence of Ein Sof, which is above even Atik.
For Atik, in and of itself,
since its matter is that it is removed and separate from the chain of descent
(Atik from the term "ne'etik" - removed24),
it is impossible for it to be drawn down below,
and in order for it to be drawn down below, it is specifically through the Essence of Ein Sof, which is not defined by any definition.
And based on this, the superiority and novelty of Yitzchak's blessing "Vayiten Lecha Elokim" over "Vayevarech Elokim es Yitzchak" will be understood,
for the blessing "Vayiten Lecha Elokim" is that there should be a drawing down below to refine the sparks that are in Eisav,
and this drawing down is from the Essence of Ein Sof,
as above.
And this is "Vayiten Lecha Elokim"
(Elokim with the definite article),
the level of the essential concealment of Ein Sof,
from which comes the power of refinements25.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The Midrash interprets "dew of heaven" as Scripture, "fat of the land" as Mishnah, and "grain" as Talmud, which is understood to mean that Yitzchak's blessing was for toil in Torah, through which one reaches above the Torah as it is in itself, up to the essential concealment, as in "No eye has seen a God besides You."
section.t: And this is26 what is stated in the Midrash27
"Dew of heaven" — this is Scripture, and "fat of the land" — this is Mishnah, "grain" — this is Talmud, etc.,
for at first glance it is not understood,
for even without Yitzchak's blessing, the Torah would have been given to Israel,
since the purpose of creation was for Israel to receive the Torah, and the Holy One, blessed be He, made a condition with the act of Creation, etc., "If Israel accepts the Torah, etc."28,
and what is it that he blessed him with Torah?
And the explanation of this is known,
that Yitzchak's blessing was concerning the matter of toil in Torah, through which one reaches a level above the Torah as it is in itself.
For the Torah in itself is the wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He,
and higher still — Chochmah Setima'ah (Concealed Wisdom),
and through toil in Torah,
toil in the manner of Or Chozer (Returning Light),
one reaches the essential concealment
(of the Torah),
"No eye29
has seen a God besides You."
